newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish marines to leave for Albania on Sunday.
newsitem.headline: Turkish marines to leave for Albania on Sunday.

text.p: More than 500 Turkish marines will leave on Sunday to join the multinational force protecting humanitarian relief operations in Albania, military headquarters said in a statement on Tuesday.
The marines were to leave for Albania by sea and air on April 20 from the western Turkish resort of Foca on the Aegean coast, the statement said.
Earlier, Defence Minister Turhan Tayan told reporters before a meeting with Albanian Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj that the unit would arrive in Albania on April 25.
Vukaj said his country was willing to work with Turkey for a peaceful and stable Balkans. "Our most important target is to increase friendship in the Balkans," he said.
The defence ministry official said between 500 to 800 marines would be sent to Albania but added it was not clear yet which part of the country they would be deployed in.

Turkey's parliament last week voted to approve a government plan to join the Italian-led peacekeeping force. Hundreds of French and Italian troops reached Tirana airport and the main port of Durres on Tuesday as the mission to protect aid convoys began.
The rest of the 6,000-strong multinational force, involving troops from Italy, France, Spain, Turkey, Greece and Romania is expected to arrive in Albania in the next two weeks.

Albania, Europe's poorest country, plunged into near chaos when get-rich-quick pyramid investment schemes collapsed and armed rebels took control of the south during an initially unchecked spasm of looting and bandity.
